back: The encoder compresses the past into a state. The decoder uses it to write the future, one step at a time.
During training the decoder gets the real previous value, not its own guess. It is stable but causes exposure bias.

front: How does DeepAR make a probabilistic forecast?
back: An LSTM outputs distribution parameters each step. We sample many paths, feeding samples back, and read quantiles.
0.5·log(2π·σ²) + (y − μ)² / (2σ²). Low when mu is close to y and sigma matches the real error.

front: Which distribution fits count data in DeepAR?
back: The negative binomial. A normal can give negative values and fits many-zero counts poorly.
